newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters in controversy over "scuffle" in bar.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters in controversy over "scuffle" in bar.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters, responding to allegations that he scuffled with a journalist in a Wellington restaurant, said on Wednesday that he had been insulted.

"For goodness sake, the day I can't go to a restaurant without being insulted by a person from the media, then things have reached a parlous state, and that is exactly what happened. I told him to run along," Peters told Reuters.

Peters, who was absent from coalition talks with the caretaker National Party on Wednesday morning and the Labour Party in the afternoon, said he had not been scheduled to attend them and had been involved in other coalition work.

Wellington restaurant manager John McGrath said earlier that Peters was involved in several incidents including a scuffle at the opening of the Brava restaurant in the early hours of Wednesday morning.

McGrath said Peters and another man, who appeared to know him, began shouting heatedly at each other and had to be broken up. "It was a push, it wasn't a punch-up," McGrath told Reuters. "A lot of people saw it."
He said the restaurant was packed at the time, with patrons spilling out into the street.
John Crowley, editor of the New Zealand Press Association, confirmed he had spoken to Peters at the restaurant but denied there had been any "fracas".

"I know of no fracas. It seems to be growing by the minute. It was suggested there was pushing and shoving, which is wrong. It was suggested there was an altercation, and that was wrong," he said. Crowley declined to comment on the alleged insult.
The New Zealand First negotiating team was led by Peters' deputy Tau Henare at Wednesday's meetings.
McGrath said Peters was with a group including former Labour Party leader Mike Moore and other MPs from both parties. McGrath said no one appeared to get hurt.
However, after the first incident, Peters got into an argument with a young woman and later still became involved in an argument with another man.
"There was another fight when he (Peters) left. He hurled abuse at a woman, then he got involved with another guy -- he was very stroppy. We kicked him out," McGrath said.
Another witness, also involved with the restaurant, but who declined to be identified, confirmed McGrath's account. Labour's Moore declined to comment.
